newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila warns against base conversion extension.
newsitem.headline: Manila warns against base conversion extension.

text.p: Philippine government lawyers said on Tuesday they had advised the Bases Conversion Development Authority (Basecon) not to formally extend a deadline for the signing of a lease agreement for Camp John Hay with Philippine-Thai consortium ML&H Corp.

Doing so "would substantially and plainly amend and/or modify the Terms of Reference, and render BCDA vulnerable to legal suits by other bidders", Pilipinas Laborte, assistant government corporate counsel, said in a statement.

Basecon's nine-man board is scheduled to meet tonight to decide whether to formally extend the September 8 deadline after Basecon and ML&H officials on Monday failed to settle a dispute over the area to be covered by the lease. Basecon is a government agency tasked with privatising former military sites.
ML&H bid 1.58 billion pesos to develop and operate Camp John Hay, a former base in the northern Philippine hill resort of Baguio. Its bid was about four times bigger than the next offer.
ML&H refused to sign the lease, saying that only 121.77 hectares of land was available for development and not the 247 hectares mentioned in the bid documents.
The ML&H consortium comprises Thailand's Land and Houses Plc, AB Capital and Asia-Pacific and Planning Evaluation Co.
